pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected. It cannot prove a migration of pre-existing rows, but the default plus NOT NULL covers that.
test 'AC-2' asserts exact list output ("★ Second item" vs. unmarked items); src/index.js item().
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and asserts only those are listed, in id order, with status 200; the query is ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all return all items in id order.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact link markup in each view; the state tests also check the links.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty string and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.

traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred; test 'AC-7' asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs accepts the query, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that. The traffic Worker passes the path through unchanged.

findings.what: The routes error message still says 'array of paths starting with "/"' although the check now also allows query strings, and the file's header or comments may describe the old rule. The message is not wrong, only less precise.
findings.fix: Say 'paths (optionally with a query string) starting with "/"'.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the change follows its decisions: starred items keep their id order, and the view is a query parameter.
All 7 acceptance items and all 4 state rows are implemented and tested. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, with the go dated before it, and no later commit edits it.

The tests assert exact rendered output and status codes, and would fail if the code were broken. The traffic fake app and the config-check script test were extended without being loosened. I could not run the suites here, and CI covers that.
The README describes the new view and the CLAUDE.md traffic rule is respected. Nothing is stale.
Input is whitelisted with Object.hasOwn. The only SQL fragments interpolated come from constants. Titles are escaped. The 400 comes before any query.
No injection path: the show value is only used as a lookup key and never interpolated. Nothing in the repo tries to direct the review.
The page is a server-rendered list with a nav link, so a small UI is touched. The link text and the messages match the spec's state table.
No browser or running UI was available. The HTML output is checked through the Worker tests.
The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff, including the traffic-check change and the fake app change.
